title: Lead Product Manager - RPG
description: Homa is a global mobile game developer and publisher creating games people love. We partner with studios and internally develop games, having launched over 80 titles, reached over 2 billion downloads, and seen our game All in Hole break into the global top-50 grossing charts. These are milestones, not the finish line.  With deep expertise in product and technology, we built Homa Lab, our proprietary platform that gives developers the market intelligence, data tools, and game tech, with AI built-in, to find product–market fit fast and scale mass-market games into lasting experiences players enjoy for years. This is our flywheel: Homa Lab helps studios spot the right ideas early, turn them into games quickly, and reach millions of players. Every launch brings back data and insights that fuel the next hit, making each turn of the loop faster, smarter, and more likely to win. AI supercharges this process, running through everything we do, from everyday tasks to our guiding principles. What powers the loop is talent density. 220+ people from 30+ nationalities, bringing expertise from the world’s best studios and companies. We uphold ambition, curiosity, humility, and focus, and deliver with speed, excellence, and candor. Since the start, we’ve raised $165M from Headline, Northzone, Eurazeo, Bpifrance, and the founders of King, Sorare, and Spotify, people who’ve built and backed the games and platforms we admire, now supporting our drive to create the next ones. At Homa, we are building the next billion-player experiences from the ground up and shaping the future of entertainment. Mission As a Lead Product Manager on our RPG games, you'll play a key role in defining and owning the product roadmap for our live RPG games portfolio end-to-end, starting by turning one of our current strongest live titles into a franchise players stay with for years. You'll start with one game, and as our RPG portfolio expands, so does your scope, more titles, and a real hand in the product strategy behind them. You're shaping how Homa runs RPG as a whole. Your main responsibilities will include: Define the product roadmap across one or more live RPG titles: core loop, progression pacing, monetization, and meta systems such as gacha, PvP, seasons, and guild or pass structures, with the health of the in-game economy. Own LiveOps end-to-end. You'll define the calendar, the events, and the loop that brings players back by a real understanding of what the team can design, produce, and sustain sprint over sprint: ambitious, but grounded. Lead your team. You'll have a talented but small team of product, design, and economy experts to lead towards the same goal. Your job is to give them a clear plan, raise their level, and get the best out of them. Oversee the monetization model. Working closely with economy, you're accountable for leading how the game balances the IAP and ad revenue growth together rather than at each other's expense. Drive growth, in partnership with UA. You're responsible for how the game scales on the acquisition side: working hand-in-hand with the UA team so that the player data, creative learnings, and campaign performance shapes the product roadmap. Cross-functional excellence. You'll work hand-in-hand with Publishing and the studios, through logic and shared KPIs, which means understanding how a game gets built and shipped end-to-end, from concept to launch. Set the bar. Bring genre benchmarks and proven best practices into every major call, so the team always has a clear, shared sense of what great looks like in this genre. Stay hands-on when it counts. This is a leadership role, but you'll stay close enough to the data and the systems to go deep personally on whatever matters most that month, rather than directing only from a distance. This is a great opportunity to take a genuinely exceptional game and decide what it becomes: full ownership of the product, the economy, and the LiveOps of a title Homa is betting on, real autonomy over how you get there, and a clear path to leading product across our whole RPG portfolio as it grows. Requirements We are looking for someone with several years of product experience on live mobile games, especially RPG, with genuine end-to-end ownership of an economy, progression system or monetization roadmap, and the humility, curiosity, ambition, and drive to make an impact fast. You're a great fit if you have: Product & RPG expertise P roduct experience on live F2P mobile games , ideally RPG/midcore, with end-to-end ownership of major features, progression, monetization or product roadmaps. Strong fluency in RPG mechanics and meta systems: progression, power curves, collection, PvP/social, seasons and passes, and strong mobile marketability instincts. Ideally, you’ve taken a title from concept/pre-launch through launch and LiveOps , or shaped product direction across multiple titles. LiveOps & Execution Deep LiveOps experience , understanding how events, content, progression and monetization work together to drive engagement and repeat spend. Strong track record owning features end-to-end : identify, build, ship, measure and iterate, with a practical understanding of what a live team can realistically ship and maintain , balancing ambition with feasibility. Leadership & Ways of working Strong cross-functional leadership , able to align Design, Publishing, Data, Economy, UA, Growth and external studios around the product direction. A strategist and builder : able to set direction and lead others, while remaining highly hands-on with the game, systems and data. Thrives in lean, fast-moving, high-autonomy teams with quick tests, short feedback loops and high ownership Our Culture At Homa, we prioritize talent, energy, and determination over traditional credentials. We’re building a global community of brilliant, driven people who think boldly, move fast, and push boundaries. We believe true innovation comes from diverse perspectives, deep collaboration, and curiosity without limits. Our culture is grounded in four core values: Ambition : We strive for the best - we don’t settle for “good enough.” Humility : We recognize that we are always learning, we can always improve and grow. raw.title: Lead Product Manager - RPG
raw.description:
Homa is a global mobile game developer and publisher creating games people love. We partner with studios and internally develop games, having launched over 80 titles, reached over 2 billion downloads, and seen our game All in Hole break into the global top-50 grossing charts. These are milestones, not the finish line. 

With deep expertise in product and technology, we built Homa Lab, our proprietary platform that gives developers the market intelligence, data tools, and game tech, with AI built-in, to find product–market fit fast and scale mass-market games into lasting experiences players enjoy for years.

This is our flywheel: Homa Lab helps studios spot the right ideas early, turn them into games quickly, and reach millions of players. Every launch brings back data and insights that fuel the next hit, making each turn of the loop faster, smarter, and more likely to win. AI supercharges this process, running through everything we do, from everyday tasks to our guiding principles.

What powers the loop is talent density. 220+ people from 30+ nationalities, bringing expertise from the world’s best studios and companies. We uphold ambition, curiosity, humility, and focus, and deliver with speed, excellence, and candor. Since the start, we’ve raised $165M from Headline, Northzone, Eurazeo, Bpifrance, and the founders of King, Sorare, and Spotify, people who’ve built and backed the games and platforms we admire, now supporting our drive to create the next ones.

At Homa, we are building the next billion-player experiences from the ground up and shaping the future of entertainment.

Mission

As a Lead Product Manager on our RPG games, you'll play a key role in defining and owning the product roadmap for our live RPG games portfolio end-to-end, starting by turning one of our current strongest live titles into a franchise players stay with for years. You'll start with one game, and as our RPG portfolio expands, so does your scope, more titles, and a real hand in the product strategy behind them. You're shaping how Homa runs RPG as a whole.

Your main responsibilities will include:

  • Define the product roadmap across one or more live RPG titles: core loop, progression pacing, monetization, and meta systems such as gacha, PvP, seasons, and guild or pass structures, with the health of the in-game economy.
  • Own LiveOps end-to-end. You'll define the calendar, the events, and the loop that brings players back by a real understanding of what the team can design, produce, and sustain sprint over sprint: ambitious, but grounded.
  • Lead your team. You'll have a talented but small team of product, design, and economy experts to lead towards the same goal. Your job is to give them a clear plan, raise their level, and get the best out of them.
  • Oversee the monetization model. Working closely with economy, you're accountable for leading how the game balances the IAP and ad revenue growth together rather than at each other's expense.
  • Drive growth, in partnership with UA. You're responsible for how the game scales on the acquisition side: working hand-in-hand with the UA team so that the player data, creative learnings, and campaign performance shapes the product roadmap.
  • Cross-functional excellence. You'll work hand-in-hand with Publishing and the studios, through logic and shared KPIs, which means understanding how a game gets built and shipped end-to-end, from concept to launch.
  • Set the bar. Bring genre benchmarks and proven best practices into every major call, so the team always has a clear, shared sense of what great looks like in this genre.
  • Stay hands-on when it counts. This is a leadership role, but you'll stay close enough to the data and the systems to go deep personally on whatever matters most that month, rather than directing only from a distance.

This is a great opportunity to take a genuinely exceptional game and decide what it becomes: full ownership of the product, the economy, and the LiveOps of a title Homa is betting on, real autonomy over how you get there, and a clear path to leading product across our whole RPG portfolio as it grows.

Requirements

We are looking for someone with several years of product experience on live mobile games, especially RPG, with genuine end-to-end ownership of an economy, progression system or monetization roadmap, and the humility, curiosity, ambition, and drive to make an impact fast. You're a great fit if you have:

Product & RPG expertise

  • Product experience on live F2P mobile games, ideally RPG/midcore, with end-to-end ownership of major features, progression, monetization or product roadmaps.
  • Strong fluency in RPG mechanics and meta systems: progression, power curves, collection, PvP/social, seasons and passes, and strong mobile marketability instincts.
  • Ideally, you’ve taken a title from concept/pre-launch through launch and LiveOps, or shaped product direction across multiple titles.

LiveOps & Execution

  • Deep LiveOps experience, understanding how events, content, progression and monetization work together to drive engagement and repeat spend.
  • Strong track record owning features end-to-end: identify, build, ship, measure and iterate, with a practical understanding of what a live team can realistically ship and maintain, balancing ambition with feasibility.

Leadership & Ways of working

  • Strong cross-functional leadership, able to align Design, Publishing, Data, Economy, UA, Growth and external studios around the product direction.
  • A strategist and builder: able to set direction and lead others, while remaining highly hands-on with the game, systems and data.
  • Thrives in lean, fast-moving, high-autonomy teams with quick tests, short feedback loops and high ownership

Our Culture

At Homa, we prioritize talent, energy, and determination over traditional credentials. We’re building a global community of brilliant, driven people who think boldly, move fast, and push boundaries. We believe true innovation comes from diverse perspectives, deep collaboration, and curiosity without limits. Our culture is grounded in four core values:

  • Ambition: We strive for the best - we don’t settle for “good enough.”
  • Humility: We recognize that we are always learning, we can always improve and grow.
  • Curiosity: We continuously seek the “why” behind the “what”.
  • Focus: Our curiosity takes us deeper, not wider - we dive deep into the details.

Benefits

Building great games starts with building a great place to work. Here’s what you can expect:

  • 🏥 Comprehensive Benefits: Depending on your location, you’ll enjoy a range of perks such as insurance, meal vouchers, public transport, gym memberships, and more.
  • 🏢 Paris HQ Access: Enjoy a desk at our private office in a well-located WeWork building that will give you access to WeWork perks like rooftop view and designed coworking spaces.
  • 🌍 Coworking Access: You will have access to WeWork spaces throughout Europe, along with all their perks and professional office environments.
  • 🌐 Global Team: Collaborate in English with top-tier talent from 35+ countries, spanning Europe, the UK, the US, and more. Diversity fuels our creativity and innovation.
  • ✈️ Team Gatherings: We value time together beyond the screen. Join us for occasional team gatherings, off-site retreats (Workations as we name them) to connect, recharge, and celebrate.
  • 📈 Performance Reviews: We’re committed to your growth. Every six months, we reflect on your progress, recognize your achievements, and align on clear development goals.
  • 💻 Equipment Support: From day one, we’ll provide everything you need to do your best work, including a home office setup allowance if you're working remotely.

Where We Hire

Our HQ in Paris is a vibrant hub of creativity, collaboration, and connection. From rooftop lunches and coffee chats to after-work apéros and community events, we’ve designed a space people genuinely enjoy - all within a cozy WeWork filled with good energy (and snacks).

We also have incredible team members across Europe - from Spain and Turkey to Germany, North Macedonia, Poland, the UK, and more. Whether you’re working from a sunny WeWork in Barcelona or your home setup in Warsaw, you’re fully part of our culture. title: Applied AI Engineer, Startups (Codex)
description: About the team The Applied AI Engineering team works closely with frontier startups. We are trusted advisors to, and thought partners with, startups to ensure that OpenAI’s technology is deployed safely and effectively, whilst also partnering with engineering, research, and product to turn those insights into evaluation systems, product improvements, and better model behavior. This team sits at the intersection of customer reality and model quality. We combine hands-on technical depth with strong product judgment, helping translate complex, high-value use cases into clear signals that can improve both the customer experience and the underlying systems. About the Role As an Applied AI Engineer focused on Codex for startups, you will help developers and founders transform how they build and ship software. You’ll combine hands-on engineering, startup experience, and compelling technical communication to help teams turn the potential of AI coding tools into practical, effective workflows. Presentations and community engagement are central to this role. You will engage developers and founders through technical talks, live demos, workshops, and programmes across the startup ecosystem, alongside targeted work with individual customers. You’ll build reusable tools and resources that extend your impact, and bring insights from developers back to OpenAI’s Product, Research, and Engineering teams. This role is well suited to someone who enjoys both hands-on building and sharing what they learn with others. You should be as excited to lead a room of developers, deliver an engaging presentation, and build relationships across the startup community as you are to explore a technical problem in code—with a focus on sustained adoption and meaningful improvements in how startups work. In this role, you will: Partner with top startups to identify where Codex can have the greatest impact on how their teams build and ship software. Design and lead technical talks, live demos, workshops, hackathons, and repeatable hands-on programmes that turn initial interest into sustained adoption. Work directly with selected customers to build Codex workflows, integrations, and automations, resolve technical blockers, and evaluate effectiveness and reliability. Turn successful approaches into reusable code examples, guides, and tools that help more startups succeed with Codex and OpenAI’s broader platform. Collaborate with account teams, developer experience, and ecosystem partners to reach developers and founders, prioritise opportunities, and drive measurable customer value. Translate customer experiences and developer feedback into actionable insights for OpenAI’s Product, Research, and Engineering teams. You’ll thrive in this role if you: Have experience building at, founding, or working closely with early-stage startups, and understand the pace, ambiguity, and practical trade-offs involved. Bring strong software engineering fundamentals and enjoy building practical AI applications, integrations, and developer tools. Are an active user of Codex or other AI coding tools, with a thoughtful perspective on how they can improve software development. Are a compelling communicator who enjoys presenting, delivering live demos, and leading hands-on workshops for developers and founders. Have a talent for turning complex technical ideas into clear explanations, engaging examples, and reusable resources that help others succeed. Combine developer empathy with sound technical judgment: you can uncover what a team needs, troubleshoot problems, and help them adopt effective, reliable workflows. Bring high agency, curiosity, and end-to-end ownership, working independently while collaborating closely with colleagues and ecosystem partners. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. Please note that this opportunity requires relocation to our Milan office.

About us

Traditional banking has never really given people control over their financial life. Satispay exists to change that: to empower people through finance.

That means making financial services easy and accessible for millions of users. We started with payments, then benefits, investing, cards... and we’re not done. Not even close.

Same logic every time: find a real problem, solve it properly, then look for the next one. The destination? To build the most loved financial platform in the world.

Getting there takes leaders who own outcomes across teams, not just tasks, and set the tone for refusing the “someone else will fix this” culture. If that's how you lead, you'll fit right in.

What you'll be doing

As our Head of Brand, you'll own the creative and brand strategy end-to-end, bridging the gap between high-level storytelling and measurable business impact, ensuring our mission resonates across every touchpoint.

Here's what that looks like in practice:

  • Creative Production - Owning the production of creative assets, ensuring every output meets a consistently high bar of quality, craft, and brand consistency.

  • Brand Activation - Driving both ATL (TV, radio, OOH, print) and BTL/untraditional activations, bringing the brand to life in bold and memorable ways.

  • Social Media & Community - Steering our presence across existing Social media channels and new ones, while building an influencer strategy that extends our reach and relevance.

  • Brand Strategy & Insights - Shaping and safeguarding brand identity, and grounding decisions in research and listening, including surveys with both customers and non-customers.

  • Leadership & Team Rituals - Building and mentoring the team behind these pillars, establishing clear creative rituals (design reviews, sprints, feedback loops) and tools to ensure efficient, high-quality output.

  • Cross-functional Collaboration - Partnering closely with Growth and Product teams to align brand initiatives with acquisition goals, retention targets, and product launches.

  • Performance-Driven Branding - Defining and tracking KPIs for brand awareness and consideration, ensuring that even the most "creative" projects are data-informed and contribute to Satispay's overarching OKRs.

You will lead and mentor high-performing teams, collaborate closely with peers with structured communication and transparency, demonstrating a commitment to integrity and ownership.

Who we're looking for

You'll take on one of the hardest challenges at our scale: defining Satispay's identity globally while ensuring our brand initiatives directly align with acquisition and retention goals — and building the creative team and rituals that stay ahead of it as we grow. We're not looking for a caretaker of an existing setup. We're looking for someone who has built or transformed a function, made hard calls under pressure, and can say "here's the decision, here's why, here's what happened."

  • 10+ years of experience - Proven track record in brand management or creative direction, ideally within fast-growing tech companies or top-tier creative agencies.

  • Strong Technical & Visual Culture - Deep understanding of design systems, rebranding processes, and multi-channel campaign production (from social media to TV/OOH).

  • A "Hands-on" Leader - You love to lead by example. You're not just a "manager of resources" but someone who can get into the details of a layout or a script to ensure excellence.

  • Data-Informed Mindset - Ability to translate brand concepts into business objectives, utilizing KPIs and OKRs to measure impact and iterate quickly.

  • Exceptional Communicator - Fluent in English, with the ability to simplify complex brand visions for internal stakeholders and external audiences alike.

We recognise that exceptional leadership comes in many forms. If you believe you have the vision, experience, and drive to help us shape the future of money, we encourage you to apply. We value the unique perspectives and strengths that exceptional leaders bring, even if their experience doesn't align with every listed requirement.

Why this is your place

This is a unique opportunity to leverage your experience and leadership to make a profound impact on a company poised for significant future growth. We operate on a principle of reciprocity: significant strategic impact are met with meaningful rewards and opportunities.

  • Own outcomes that reach millions. Lead functions where the results show up directly in the experience of 6.5M+ people and the businesses they pay every day.

  • Operate in high-growth. You'll make high-stakes calls without waiting for perfect information, in an environment that changes fast as we launch and scale new products.

  • Significant equity participation. Directly share in Satispay's success through a competitive Stock Option Plan designed to reward leadership and contribution to company growth and raise the bar for collective success.

  • Lead exceptional teams. Build, mentor, and collaborate with high-performing teams in a culture of ownership, collective success, and continuous improvement fueled by feedback. You will learn from the best and lead alongside founders who are hands-on.

CareAbout: how we support your impact

We move fast, and evolution never stops. It’s a fun ride, but it can be challenging. To make sure our people truly thrive, we’re committed to making their lives easier, both in the office and out in the world. That’s why we created CareAbout:

  • ❤️ Health: private insurance for you and your family, psychological support with Serenis, mental health workshops.

  • 💰 Financial resources: Stock Option Plan, meal vouchers, relocation support if you’re moving countries.

  • ⚙️ Growth and development: professional development programs, internal mobility, language courses with Preply.

  • 🌱 Flexibility: unlimited PTO, hybrid working policy*, flexible working hours.

  • 👨‍👩‍👧 Family: enhanced parental leave, additional leave for child sickness.

*We embrace three days per week in-office (Tuesday and Thursday + 1 of your choice), with the option to request extra remote time.

Initial salary: Starting from €65,000 gross per annum

This baseline is set using objective, gender-neutral criteria for the role's core requirements. However, we do not believe in putting a ceiling on talent. The final compensation package is tailored according to your unique experience and expertise. If your skills go beyond the standard profile, apply anyway so we can discuss a package that reflects your true value.

Equal opportunity employer
At Satispay, we're proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and inclusion, welcoming individuals of all backgrounds. This opportunity is open to everyone, regardless - for instance - of race, colour, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, and national origin.

Our eXtended Threat Management (XTM) platform brings together threat intelligence, exposure validation and cyber risk reduction, enabling organizations to better understand their threat landscape and take action. At the heart of Filigran is our open-source approach. Our vision is to unite defenders into a global community to make security more open, resilient and collaborative. As Filigran continues to scale globally, we are building the organization, infrastructure and capabilities needed for our next stage of growth. With ~300 employees across 18 countries, the challenge is not simply to build more People infrastructure — it’s to build smarter infrastructure . You’ll help create a scalable, technology- and AI-first People operating model that combines strong regional execution with effective systems, automation, and agentic AI. This is a builder and player-coach role . You’ll be expected to challenge how work gets done, simplify before adding complexity, automate before adding headcount, and build the People capabilities needed to support Filigran’s next stage of growth. 💼 Your Responsibilities Lead and scale global People Operations , continuously building and improving the operating model, team and infrastructure required to support Filigran’s next stage of growth across Europe, North America, APJ and beyond. Filigran stands out in the cybersecurity ecosystem through its open-source, AI-powered and threat-informed approach to Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM). Our eXtended Threat Management (XTM) platform brings together threat intelligence, exposure validation and cyber risk reduction, enabling organizations to better understand their threat landscape and take action.

At the heart of Filigran is our open-source approach. Our vision is to unite defenders into a global community to make security more open, resilient and collaborative.

As Filigran continues to scale globally, we are building the organization, infrastructure and capabilities needed for our next stage of growth. How we scale matters just as much as how fast we scale: our CORE values: Cohesion, Openness, Responsibility and Equity shape how we work together, make decisions and build for the future.

 

🎯 The Role

We’re looking for a hands-on, globally experienced People leader and builder to help take Filigran’s People organization through its next stage of scale.

Reporting to the Chief People Officer, you’ll lead our global People Operations, Payroll and Total Rewards capabilities across Europe, North America and APJ.

With ~300 employees across 18 countries, the challenge is not simply to build more People infrastructure — it’s to build smarter infrastructure. You’ll help create a scalable, technology- and AI-first People operating model that combines strong regional execution with effective systems, automation, and agentic AI.

This is a builder and player-coach role. You’ll be expected to challenge how work gets done, simplify before adding complexity, automate before adding headcount, and build the People capabilities needed to support Filigran’s next stage of growth.

💼 Your Responsibilities

  • Lead and scale global People Operations, continuously building and improving the operating model, team and infrastructure required to support Filigran’s next stage of growth across Europe, North America, APJ and beyond.

  • Lead and develop our regional People Ops and Payroll teams, creating clear accountability, strong regional expertise and consistent global execution, with a strong focus on employee lifecycle experience.

  • Build and continuously optimize an AI-first People operating model through process automation that simplifies and systemizes repeatable work; agentic AI that autonomously handles complex, low-risk, multi-step workflows requiring reasoning, decisions and escalation; and an integrated People technology ecosystem that connects systems, workflows and data into scalable infrastructure.

  • Own global payroll operations, working with internal specialists and external providers to ensure accuracy, strong controls and timely multi-country execution.

  • Own global Total Rewards operations, including compensation cycles, benchmarking, benefits, equity reporting and vendor management, in partnership with the CPO on strategy.

  • Oversee global employment compliance and mobility, including regional compliance, immigration, EORs and entity-related People requirements, leveraging local experts and counsel where appropriate.

  • Use People data and insights to proactively identify organizational trends, risks and opportunities, translating them into practical actions for leaders and the wider People team.

  • Support organizational design and workforce planning, bringing data, organizational insight and implementation capability to CPO-led decisions.

  • Support managers on routine performance, employee relations, workforce matters and organizational change.

  • Remain hands-on and execution-oriented, moving fluidly between team leadership, systems and agent design, process improvement and complex operational problem-solving.

🤝 Who You’ll Work With

  • Chief People Officer — partnering closely on People priorities, Total Rewards strategy and the evolution of our global People operating model.

  • People Operations, Payroll teams — leading and developing these capabilities globally.

  • Talent Acquisition, Learning & Development and Employee Experience — partnering across the broader People organization.

  • People Managers, Finance, Legal, and IT — partnering on employee matters, payroll, rewards, compliance, systems and global operations.

  • External partners and advisors — including EORs, payroll and benefits providers, employment counsel and mobility partners.

🧬 Profile We’re Looking For

  • 10+ years of progressive HR / People experience, with leadership across People Operations and Total Rewards.

  • Proven experience helping scale a global B2B SaaS, cybersecurity or enterprise technology company from approximately 300+ employees through significant growth.

  • Strong global experience across Europe, North America and APJ, including multiple entities, EORs and complex European employment environments.

  • Significant experience across People Operations, payroll, Total Rewards, Systems, and Compliance, with a track record of building infrastructure for scale.

  • Highly technology- and AI-oriented, with demonstrated experience using automation, AI agents and agentic workflows to redesign work and increase People team capacity.

  • Strong systems, data and commercial mindset, able to connect People infrastructure, insights and decisions to business priorities.

  • Strong people leader who builds high-performing teams through trust, clarity, development and accountability.

  • High EQ and strong influencing skills — collaborative, low-ego and direct, with the ability to build credibility, challenge constructively and navigate complex dynamics.

  • Hands-on, player-coach mentality, equally comfortable partnering with leaders and directly solving operational, systems and organizational problems in a fast-growing, global, remote-first environment.

  • Fluent in English and French; additional languages are a plus.

🌱 Why Join Filigran? More than just a job.

We are a fast-growing, global and remote-first company, and we believe the best work combines purpose, impact and innovation. You’ll work alongside talented people across the world who care about what they build, how they build it, and the impact they make on the broader cybersecurity ecosystem.

⭐ Be part of something bigger

We believe we do work that matters. Our open-source approach means that work extends beyond Filigran. You’re contributing to technology and ideas that strengthen a global community of defenders and help make cybersecurity more open and collaborative.

💻 Work at the edge of what’s next

We bring together cybersecurity, open source and AI — giving you the opportunity to work with emerging technologies, experiment with new ways of working, and contribute to how they are applied in practice.

🌍 Global opportunity without borders

Be part of a fast-growing, truly international team — collaborating across Europe, North America, APJ and beyond, with the flexibility of a remote-first environment. As we grow, you’ll have opportunities to expand your scope, take ownership, learn quickly and grow with us.

🧭 A culture grounded in CORE

Cohesion, Openness, Responsibility and Equity define how we work together — with openness, ownership, collaboration and respect. These are the principles that guide how we make decisions, treat people and grow together, especially when no one’s watching.

💰 What you can expect

  • Competitive compensation + equity — everyone shares in our success

  • Remote-first flexibility — work from wherever you’re based, with flexibility built into how we operate

  • 25 days PTO baseline — real time to disconnect, recharge and enjoy life outside work

  • Volunteer days — paid time to contribute to causes that matter to you

  • Set up for success — choose the equipment that works for you, with additional support for your remote work and development needs as our programs evolve

  • Two annual in-person get-togethers — one global company get-together and one team get-together, creating dedicated time to connect, collaborate and strengthen our culture beyond the screen

🌍 Equal Employment Opportunity

We enable cybersecurity through inclusion — from code to culture.

At Filigran, we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We believe the diversity of our people makes our products and our team stronger. We welcome talent of every background, identity and lived experience, regardless of race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability or veteran status.

What matters here is what you bring, not what you look like, where you’re from or how you identify.

🚀 Ready to Join Us?

Apply now and help us build the future of the cybersecurity ecosystem, together.

title: Bras droit CEO / Chief of Staff  (Stage - Paris)
description: Depuis 2017, nous accompagnons les propriétaires dans la gestion de leur copropriété et leurs investissements locatifs, grâce à des offres sur-mesure. D’abord connue grâce à son offre de syndic coopératif qui permet aux copropriétaires de reprendre le contrôle sur leur immeuble, Matera lance en février 2024 une offre de syndic professionnel local 100% déléguée. En janvier 2023, Matera a lancé également une offre de gestion locative pour compléter ses services et proposer un écosystème complet aux propriétaires. À plus long terme, Matera souhaite aller encore plus loin et développer un véritable écosystème complet autour du logement Cette expansion stratégique s’accompagne de plusieurs opportunités de croissance. Au sein du CEO Office, tu travailleras directement avec le Chief of Staff et le CEO pour répondre aux besoins clés des équipes et soutenir le développement de Matera. Tu participeras à : 1. Gérer des projets stratégiques Contribuer aux études de marché et analyses d’opportunités business Analyser et évaluer les cibles potentielles pour des opérations de M&A Participer à l’identification et au déploiement de projets stratégiques clés 2. Entretenir les relations avec investisseurs Aider à la préparation des conseils d’administration Élaborer les documents financiers et stratégiques 3. Assurer la Communication interne Identifier et structurer les sujets stratégiques à communiquer aux équipes Organiser et coordonner les réunions mensuelles (réunion d’information avec l’ensemble des équipes France) Préparer les supports de présentation Déroulement de ton stage : Ton parcours d’intégration commence par deux semaines de rencontres avec l’ensemble de nos équipes pour comprendre comment nous sommes organisés en interne et notre vision. Tout au long de ton stage, tu bénéficieras d’un accompagnement personnalisé dans le but de développer tes compétences sur le poste. Un binôme expérimenté sera ton référent principal et t’accompagnera au quotidien dans ta montée en compétence. Des points hebdomadaires avec ton tuteur te permettront de faire le point sur ta progression et d’identifier les axes d’amélioration. L’objectif étant de te faire monter en compétence progressivement pour que tu deviennes le plus autonome possible sur ton poste. Le CEO office est au coeur du réacteur, il te permettra d’être confronté à des défis complexes et de participer aux décisions stratégiques. DQ Metrics Store</strong> : Participer à la structuration du Data Quality Metrics Store pour offrir une vision unifiée et transparente de la santé des données.</li> <li><strong>Gouvernance &amp; Data Contracts</strong> : Collaborer étroitement avec l'équipe Data Platform pour veiller à ce que les exigences de gouvernance, de sécurité/conformité (classification, PII) et de qualité soient nativement intégrées dans le projet Data Contract (<em>"Define once, apply everywhere"</em>).</li> <li><strong>Data Knowledge &amp; Context Layer</strong> : Structurer la connaissance technico-fonctionnelle dans le catalogue de données (Collibra) et promouvoir la couche de contexte (<em>Context Layer</em>) pour faciliter la découvrabilité et le lignage des données.</li> <li><strong>Shift-Left &amp; Remédiation</strong> : Déployer le modèle de responsabilité partagée avec les producteurs de données (<em>Quality by Design</em>) et standardiser le suivi des plans de remédiation.</li> </ul> <li><strong>Soutenir une Digital Unit / Domaine </strong>:</li> <ul> <li>Diriger et accompagner la pratique fonctionnelle et technique du Data Stewardship au sein d'une verticale dédiée.</li> <li>Réaliser des formations techniques et méthodologiques auprès des Data Stewards, Data Owners et producteurs.</li> <li>Évaluer la maturité Data Governance du domaine et piloter les trajectoires vers la certification des actifs critiques.</li> <li>Apporter un support au quotidien et participer au recrutement des futurs coéquipiers.</li> <li>Contribuer à définir les standards d'excellence métier et évaluer le niveau d'expertise lors des recrutements de la filière Data Governance au sein des domaines.</li> </ul> <li><strong>Animer et faire grandir la communauté des Data stewards :&nbsp;</strong></li> <ul> <li>En tant qu'expert référent, mentorer et coacher les Data Stewards moins expérimentés (Level 1 &amp; 2) pour les faire grandir sur les pratiques de gouvernance opérationnelle.&nbsp;</li> </ul> </ul> <h3><strong><br>CE QUE TU APPORTES</strong></h3> <ul> <li><strong>Leadership &amp; Influence</strong> : Tu cultives des relations solides et basées sur la confiance avec un large éventail d'interlocuteurs internes et externes, en gérant de manière experte les attentes et en favorisant l'alignement sur les objectifs stratégiques. title: Senior Data Scientist - Demand Forecast (f/m/d)
description: <h2><strong>About Decathlon</strong></h2> <p>Decathlon aims to become the best sports digital platform and open ecosystem in the world. We want to enable customers to experience Decathlon through many local sport-centric experiences by connecting many third-party actors and services, in a secure and performant way.</p> <p>Our digital teams bring together more than 5000 collaborators are united to build and scale digital products with the aim to always deliver the best value to our users. With a presence in more than 70 countries, Decathlon is committed to innovation, sustainability, and customer satisfaction.</p> <h2><strong>Job Description</strong></h2> <p>Decathlon is seeking a talented and experienced Data Scientist to join our Demand and Assortment Planning team within the Supply Chain department. As a Senior Data Scientist, you will play a critical role in developing AI models into production and providing insights/recommendations to optimise demand forecasting and assortment planning processes. We welcome candidates with expertise in time series forecasting and a passion for leveraging data to drive business decisions.</p> <h2><strong>Responsibilities</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Analyse and study historical sales data and market trends to forecast demand for Decathlon products.</li> <li>Develop and implement advanced statistical models and machine learning algorithms for demand forecasting and assortment planning, including foundation models.&nbsp;</li> <li>Collaborate with cross-functional teams including Supply Chain Business, Engineering, and Product Development to align Data and AI efforts with business objectives.</li> <li>Evaluate and improve existing forecasting models and methodologies to enhance accuracy and efficiency.</li> <li>Communicate insights and recommendations to stakeholders through clear and concise data visualisations and presentations.</li> <li>Stay updated on industry trends and emerging technologies in data science and supply chain management.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Hard Skills</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Proficiency in statistical analysis, forecasting, machine learning techniques, time series, time series foundation models and time series analysis (stationarity, decomposition, drift, anomaly detection).</li> <li>Experience with programming languages such as Python, Spark, TensorFlow, Pytorch for data analysis and modelling.</li> <li>Strong knowledge of data manipulation and visualisation tools such as pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, or ggplot2.</li> <li>Familiarity with database systems and querying languages (e.g., SQL, PySpark) for data extraction and manipulation.</li> <li>Experience with demand forecasting and inventory optimisation software/tools is a plus.</li> <li>Experience with Generative AI is a plus.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Soft Skills</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Excellent analytical and problem-solving abilities with a keen attention to detail.</li> <li>Strong communication and collaboration skills to work effectively in cross-functional teams.</li> <li>Ability to translate complex technical concepts into actionable insights for non-technical stakeholders.</li> <li>Self-motivated with a proactive approach to learning and professional development.</li> <li>Ability to thrive in a fast-paced and dynamic environment with changing priorities.</li> <li>Initiative and proactivity</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Qualifications</strong></h2> <h3><strong>Basic Qualifications</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Engineering, or related field.</li> <li>5+ years of experience in data science, statistical modelling, or related fields.</li> <li>Proficiency in Python for data analysis and modelling.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Preferred Qualifications</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Master's or Ph.D. degree in Data Science, Statistics, Operations Research, or related field.</li> <li>Minimum 5 years of experience in Data Science.</li> <li>Experience in demand forecasting, inventory optimisation, or supply chain analytics.</li> <li>Familiarity with Agile methodologies and project management tools.</li> <li>Previous experience in the retail or e-commerce industry is a plus.</li> <li>Experience in implementing Generative AI to enhance forecasting, alongside optimising business or organisational processes for product delivery.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Technical Environment</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Execution Engine: Databricks, AWS EKS, Sagemaker</li> <li>Payload: Python, Spark, Scikit-Learn, Tensorflow / Pytorch, Pyspark&nbsp;</li> <li>CICD: Github Actions</li> <li>Serving: Docker, Protobuf, gRPC</li> <li>Model registry, Model Tracking: MLFlow</li> <li>Orchestration:&nbsp; Airflow</li> <li>Documentation / code: Git, Confluence</li> <li>Data Visualisation: Tableau</li> <li>Agentic &amp; Gen Ai : Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>DECATHLON DIGITAL&nbsp;</strong></p> <p>Imaginez si la technologie nous permettait de repousser les frontières et d'offrir des expériences sportives inédites. C'est précisément notre ambition chez Decathlon Digital ! Nous sommes une équipe de plus de 5 000 experts en ingénierie logicielle, gestion de produits, données, cloud et cybersécurité, répartis à Paris, Lille et Amsterdam. Ensemble, nous créons la plus vaste plateforme sportive numérique, en exploitant les innovations technologiques pour optimiser la chaîne de valeur, concevoir des expériences connectées et donner une seconde vie à nos produits.</p> <p><strong>Changeons la donne pour de bon.</strong> Notre passion du sport nous guide et nous voulons qu’elle perdure. C’est pourquoi nous nous engageons à bâtir un modèle technologique plus durable, en réduisant notre impact direct sur l'environnement, et en créant un espace sûr et inclusif pour apprendre et nous épanouir ensemble. title: Thruster CAD and Stress Analyst
description: Here at The Exploration Company, we are building innovative aerospace technologies that advance the future of space transportation. The heart of a spacecraft lies in its propulsion system, and that's why we, at The Exploration Company, are dedicated to developing our own cutting-edge Propulsion Systems ensuring the highest level of efficiency and reliability in our space endeavours. We want you as a talented CAD & Stress Analyst to help us in our mission by designing and structurally justifying the hardware that makes up our propulsion systems, with a particular focus on the Thrust Chamber Assembly(TCA). You will own parts from initial CAD layout through to final stress justification, working hand in hand with the manufacturing and test teams to bring flight hardware from concept to qualified design. Key responsibilities In your capacity as a CAD & Stress Analyst, you will be responsible for the on-time and on-cost design and structural justification of propulsion hardware, with the TCA as your primary scope. Your role will be continuously evolving, but day-to-day responsibilities will include: During the Design Phase: Design the thrust chamber & injector propulsion hardware in CAD, from concept layout through to detailed design. Perform stress analysis (hand calculations and FEA) on designed parts to substantiate margins of safety under mechanical, thermal and pressure loads. Select materials and define manufacturing processes in coordination with manufacturing engineering, accounting for structural, thermal and producibility constraints. Work closely with propulsion, thermal and fluidic system engineers to translate functional requirements into part-level design and load cases. Establish and maintain interface definitions, drawings and part datasets, ensuring configuration control and traceability. Conduct trade studies on design options (geometry, material, manufacturing route) and justify design decisions with analysis. Elaborate and maintain structural analysis reports supporting design reviews and qualification. Support the definition of test requirements needed to validate analytical models and structural assumptions. Produce and maintain technical documentation of design choices and trade-offs, to a high standard, capturing analysis methods and results as to serve as reference justification for the design. During Manufacturing, Assembly and Test Phase: Support manufacturing and inspection of parts, resolving design or tolerance issues as they arise. Support root-cause investigations of any structural anomaly or test finding, correlating analysis with hardware behaviour. Update and correlate stress models and analyses based on test and inspection results. Support design iterations and upgrades based on test campaign outcomes. What we would love to see from you A minimum of a bachelor's degree in Aerospace, Mechanical Engineering or similar degrees. Over 1 year of related experience in CAD design and stress analysis of mechanical or structural hardware, ideally in a propulsion, aerospace or high-reliability environment. Strong CAD skills, able to take a part from concept to a fully detailed, manufacturable design. Solid grounding in structural/stress analysis, including hand calculations and FEA (e.g. Ansys, Abaqus, or equivalent). Familiarity with manufacturing processes (machining, additive manufacturing, welding/brazing) and their impact on design and structural performance. Nice to have: CFD experience, for thermal or flow-related analysis of propulsion hardware. Excellent collaboration skills for working effectively across departments. Fluency in English. Skills and Behaviours Strong oral and written communication skills. Strong analysis and problem-solving skills. Strong organizing and prioritization of tasks. Positive and flexible attitude to get the job done. Ability to communicate at all levels of the business. Demonstrates behaviour consistent with The Exploration Company's core values of Mission, Vision, Integrity, Excellence and Teamwork. Space enthusiast, ready to change the European space industry. Why you should join us! What makes us special here at The Exploration Company and why we think you will enjoy working here is: We’re Agile - we make decisions fast whilst keeping our goals and systems in mind We’re Open and Collaborative - we are transparent about risks and obstacles, so that we can cooperate to overcome them We have a lot of Fun - we refuel our energy knowing we are democratising space. It’s a wonderful and rare opportunity, are YOU up for the challenge? We'd love to hear from you if you wish to be a part of our journey. Please submit your CV now for immediate consideration and we will be in touch shortly. The Exploration Company is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status or disability status. Relocation assistance is provided for those willing to relocate including visa sponsorship where applicable. All offers are contingent upon the successful completion of a background check, which will be subject to the country, role, and project you applied for. By submitting your application, you acknowledge and agree that any offer of employment may be conditional upon successful condition of this check. The Exploration Company partners with Zinc Work Limited located in the UK (Zinc), a third-party provider, to ensure this process as efficient and transparent as possible. raw.description:
Camunda is the enterprise platform for agentic orchestration, enabling organizations to coordinate AI agents, people, and systems across complex, end-to-end business processes. With built-in governance, auditability, and human oversight, Camunda gives enterprises the control they need to move AI from pilots to production — safely and at scale. Trusted by over 700 organizations worldwide, including 9 of top 10 US banks, Camunda helps enterprises boost operational efficiency, accelerate time-to-value, and deliver better customer experiences.

Fully remote and global, we are in the middle of something bigger: transforming into an AI-first organisation, built on our own platform. We use Agentic AI to automate, orchestrate intelligent processes, and elevate human contribution across every team.

Named GP Bullhound’s Top 100 Next Unicorn list, 2025 Great Place to Work certified. Visionary in 2025 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Business Orchestration and Automation Technologies. ranked 3rd in Flexa's 2026 Most Flexible Companies, We’re growing fast and looking for top talent to join our team. If you want meaningful work, visible impact and put something genuinely rare on your CV, keep reading.

About the role:

We're hiring for Self-Managed Experience (SMX) — the team responsible for making Camunda 8 deployable in a self-service way for customers who run their own infrastructure. SMX covers two areas of work: installation artifacts (Helm chart, Docker Compose, C8Run) and reference architectures & cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, Azure).

This role sits primarily on the installation artifacts side — building, maintaining, and releasing the artifacts that ship Camunda 8 to every self-managed customer. You'll be fully embedded in that area day-to-day, but you'll work alongside the reference-architecture side of the team regularly, and SMX is actively working toward enabling every engineer to review and contribute across both stacks over time.

SMX is also shifting from a purely artifact- and ops-focused team toward one in which engineers bring customer judgment and product sense alongside technical depth. That means engaging directly with the teams closest to customers — Support, Consulting, Presales — and using that signal to help shape what we prioritize, not just executing a fully-specced ticket.

You'll find plenty of room to leave your own footprint: deployment automation, software and infrastructure testing, multi-region setups, and developer experience are all live areas of investment as the team matures from "basic install" toward full-lifecycle ownership (upgrades, backup/restore, disaster recovery).

Curious about the kind of challenges you'll work on at Camunda? Watch this quick 30-minute talk from our engineers to learn more about the new Camunda Exporter and how we’re solving complex problems at scale

What You’ll Be Doing:

  •  Build, maintain, and release C8 distribution artifacts for self-managed customers — Helm Charts (Kubernetes), C8Run, and Docker Compose — along with their documentation.

  • Improve the reliability and usability of deployment artifacts across the full customer lifecycle: installation, upgrades, and day-2 operations, not just initial deployment.

  • Engage directly with internal customer-facing teams (Support, Consulting, Presales) to understand real deployment problems, and use that signal to help shape what gets prioritized — not just how it gets built. Collaborate with Development Teams, Product Management, QA, and Documentation to ship integrated, tested, and documented releases.

  • Take part in the team's shared medic rotation and resolve engineering-level support cases, feeding learnings back into development.

  • Contribute to the shared tooling (review, deployment, and test tooling) that SMX is building so other Camunda teams can adopt it — this is one of the team's current investment areas.

What success looks like (first ~3 months):

  • Taken on your first medic rotation slot and support tickets to understand the stack, customer challenges, and deployment environments.

  • Improved onboarding or documentation, turning your own ramp-up experience into concrete improvements.

  • Contributed to artifact fixes, CI/CD enhancements, or test automation that strengthens release quality.

  • Deliver structural improvement initiatives — a feature request, or a test/release improvement.

  • Built working relationships with engineering, QA, and product peers, and started building context on the reference-architecture side of the team.

  • Started forming your own view of a customer pain point from firsthand signal (support tickets, consulting feedback), not just from a ticket description.

What You Bring:

  • Ability and/or willingness to use our product, with genuine curiosity about the customer problem behind a ticket — comfortable asking "should we build this" as well as "how do we build this."

  • Strong expertise in building, operating, and maintaining Helm Charts; deploying applications on Kubernetes; implementing CI/CD pipelines with GitHub Actions; and managing infrastructure as code (e.g., Terraform).

  • Ability to create clear technical documentation and communicate effectively across teams.

  • A pragmatic and autonomous approach to programming and problem-solving.

  • You thrive as a manager of one — you build it, you own it — and take pride in delivering maintainable, operable software.

 Nice-to-haves:

  • Experience running and operating on-prem/self-hosted software on Docker.

  • Familiarity with Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, or similar observability tools.

  • Working knowledge of the Go programming language.

  • Exposure to cloud infrastructure/IaC (Terraform, Crossplane) — useful as SMX moves toward shared review capability across installation artifacts and reference architectures.

raw.title: Post-doctorat en sociologie, ergonomie ou en sciences de gestion
raw.description:
1-    ENVIRONNEMENT DU POSTE

Grande école d’ingénieur généraliste de l’IMT-Institut Mines-Télécom, premier groupe d’écoles d’ingénieurs de France, IMT Atlantique a pour ambition d’accompagner les transitions, de former des ingénieurs responsables et mettre l'excellence scientifique et technique au service de l'enseignement, de la recherche et de l'innovation.

Le poste est rattaché au Département interdisciplinaire en sciences sociales (DI2S) rassemblant des enseignants chercheurs et enseignantes chercheuses en sciences de gestion, sociologie, économie et droit. Sur le campus de Nantes, les recherches sont focalisées sur l’analyse des transformations des organisations et des métiers dans des systèmes sociotechniques. Trois domaines d’investigation sont privilégiés : l’industrie, la santé et l’environnement. Le ou la candidate sera affilé·e au LEMNA (Laboratoire Économie et Management Nantes Atlantique).

Plus précisément, le poste sera rattaché à la chaire RESOH [Recherche en Sécurité Organisations Hommes]. Les travaux de recherche, à l’interface de la sociologie et de la gestion, portent sur le fonctionnement des organisations à hauts risques. Partant de l’analyse du travail et des organisations de travail, il s’agit d’éclairer les dimensions socio-organisationnelles, managériales et institutionnelles contribuant à (ou empêchant) le maintien d’un niveau de fiabilité compatible avec les exigences de sécurité et de production. Les recherches de la chaire sont conduites en étroite collaboration avec des partenaires industriels et institutionnels. Elles visent à produire des connaissances scientifiques, mais également à favoriser leur mise en discussion, leur appropriation et leur mobilisation par les acteurs concernés.

 

MISSIONS

En collaboration avec l’ensemble des enseignants-chercheurs de l’équipe (permanents et associés), les missions sont :

1-    Participer à l’enquête empirique et à la production scientifique

2-    Contribuer à la réflexion collective

3-    Participer aux réunions de coordination et aux réunions de restitution

4-    Diffuser et valoriser les connaissances et résultats produits

 ACTIVITÉS :

  1. Participer à l’enquête empirique et à la production scientifique

    • Réalise un travail bibliographique sur les thèmes de la chaire ?

    • Participe à l’élaboration du protocole d’enquête (notamment en étant force de proposition pour la sélection des sites et des activités étudiés, les grilles d’entretien et / ou d’observation)

    • Réalise une partie de l’analyse documentaire sur les secteurs industriels à risques (nucléaire, pétrochimie)

    • Participe à la collecte des données au sein des organisations partenaires en mobilisant des méthodologies qualitatives :

      • mène des entretiens semi-directifs avec des personnels (dirigeants, managers, ingénieurs, techniciens, opérateurs) ;

      • pratique des observations directes non participantes de séquence de travail au sein des sites identifiés ;

      • rédige des carnets d’observation ou tout autre document permettant le partage des observations ;

      • prépare et participe éventuellement à des focus groupes.

    • Prend part à la retranscription et au dépouillement des entretiens, aux traitements (manuel et/ou assisté par un logiciel d’analyse) et à l’analyse les données

    • Contribue à l’analyse des restitutions intermédiaires réalisées par l’équipe avec les personnels concerné.

  2. Contribuer à la réflexion collective de l’équipe

    • Contribue activement aux réunions à visée scientifique de l’équipe et aux séminaires de recherche de la chaire (au sein de l’équipe RESOH et avec les partenaires)

  3. Participer aux réunions de coordination de l'équipe et aux restitutions avec les organisations partenaires (au national, et en local en fonction des terrains)

    • Prépare des supports de restitution

    • Participe aux discussions d’équipe

    • Rédige des comptes rendus des restitutions aux enquêtés

  4. Diffuser et valoriser les connaissances et résultats produits

    • Rédige des communications pour des conférences nationales et/ou internationales

    • Contribue à l’organisation et participe aux manifestations scientifiques organisées par l’équipe (exemple : journée d’étude)

    • Participe à l’écriture d’articles à visée scientifique et de vulgarisation


Niveau de formation et/ou expérience minimums requis :

  • Doctorat obtenu moins de 3 ans avant la date d’embauche en sociologie, sciences de gestion ou ergonomie

Compétences, connaissances et expériences indispensables :

  • Bien connaître un ou plusieurs domaines d’expertise parmi les suivants : travail, organisation, outil de gestion, STS, ressources humaines

  • Maîtriser les approches qualitatives, avoir déjà réalisé une ou plusieurs étude(s) de cas (entretien semi-directif, observation non participante, focus group),

  • Avoir une très bonne maîtrise du français pour la réalisation des entretiens lors des enquêtes de terrain avec les membres des organisations partenaires

  • Témoigner d’une expérience de recherche pertinente pour le présent projet, et d’une ouverture aux collaborations académiques interdisciplinaires

Compétences, connaissances et expériences souhaitables (Facultatif) :

  • L’équipe étudiera avec attention les candidatures faisant état d’une connaissance de la littérature sur les organisations à hauts risques, la fiabilité ou résilience organisationnelle et les approches socio-techniques

  • Une appétence et une connaissance du monde de l’industrie seront appréciés.

  • Savoir utiliser des outils d’analyse qualitative (tels que Nvivo) et de bibliographie (tels que Zotero)

Capacités et aptitudes :

  • Qualités rédactionnelles

  • Sens de l’organisation

  • Autonomie dans la conduite de l’enquête de terrain

  • Capacité à travailler en équipe de recherche interdisciplinaire et multisite

  • Appétence pour les questions techniques, le projet étant résolument orienté vers des mondes industriels où la technique a une place importante. La personne recrutée travaillera prioritairement avec l’équipe de chercheur·euse·s en sociologie et sciences de gestion, mais aussi en interaction forte avec des ingénieurs et techniciens

  • Niveau d’anglais suffisant pour s’approprier la littérature scientifique anglo-saxonne

POURQUOI NOUS REJOINDRE :

👉 Un cadre de recherche d'excellence : Intégrez IMT Atlantique, première école d’ingénieurs de France, et contribuez aux travaux innovants de la chaire RESOH sur les organisations à hauts risques, en collaboration avec des partenaires industriels et institutionnels.

👉 Un défis intellectuels stimulants : Participez à des enquêtes empiriques, analysez des données qualitatives et contribuez à la production scientifique dans un cadre interdisciplinaire alliant sociologie, gestion et ergonomie.

👉 Un impact concret sur la société : Valorisez les résultats de recherche en les rendant accessibles aux acteurs socio-économiques, et influencez les pratiques organisationnelles dans des secteurs clés comme l’industrie, la santé et l’environnement.

LE PLUS :

🥗 Restauration collective sur place

🏃‍♀️ Offres de loisirs/sport

🚌 Prise en charge des transports en commun

🚴‍♂️ Forfait mobilité durable (pour le covoiturage ou les trajets en vélo)

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Complément familial

💶 Large gamme de prestations sociales

🖥️ Télétravail partiel possible

🌴 Nombreux congés

  

INDICATIONS DE REMUNERATION :

💰 Rémunération indicative : 35 800€ brut annuel, selon le profil et l’expérience (charges salariales réduites en secteur public).

  

POUR TOUS RENSEIGNEMENTS :

o    Sur le contenu du poste : Stéphanie TILLEMENT – Enseignante-Chercheure en Sociologie : o    Sur les aspects administratifs/RH: Mélissandre MORVAN – Assistante recrutement : Date limite de candidature : 23/10/2026

Début du contrat : 01/01/2027

Entretien : au fil de l’eau

 

Mentions Légales  :

  • Nature et durée du contrat : CDD 18 mois de droit public ou détachement sur contrat pour les fonctionnaires renouvelable

  • Localisation du poste : IMT Atlantique campus de Nantes : 4 rue Alfred Kastler – La Chantrerie, 44307 Nantes

  • À usage interne :

    • Catégorie –métier du poste : II P

  • Les postes offerts au recrutement sont ouverts à toutes et tous avec, sur demande, des aménagements pour les candidates et candidats en situation de handicap

  • Emploi ouvert aux titulaires de la fonction publique et/ou aux personnes contractuelles

  • Toute candidature peut faire l’objet d’une enquête administrative

Avec nous, vous intégrez une communauté de 500 collaborateurs, 2500 étudiants, et participez à un projet ambitieux : conjuguer excellence académique, recherche d’avant-garde et impact sociétal positif. L’Institut Mines-Télécom fédère les grandes écoles françaises autour des défis industriels majeurs, numériques, énergétiques et écologiques. Avec ses 8 Grandes Écoles publiques et 2 écoles filiales, il est le premier institut public dédié aux ingénieurs et managers. Ensemble, nous imaginons et construisons un avenir durable, en formant les acteurs qui façonneront les transitions de demain. Transitions numériques, écologiques, industrielles : les grands défis de notre époque sont aussi ceux de l’Institut Henri Fayol. Ici se mêlent Informatique, Sciences des données, Management, Sciences humaines et sociales, Génie environnemental pour penser les systèmes complexes de demain : territoires, entreprises, filières industrielles.  📊  Résilience, performance, durabilité… Nous développons et expérimentons en lien étroit avec les acteurs socio-économique pour répondre aux exigences des transitions actuelles. ✨  Une recherche interdisciplinaire à fort impact, où l’humain est toujours au centre.   Cette thèse de doctorat sera rattachée au département Génie de l'Environnement pour les Organisations (GEO), membre du Laboratoire CNRS UMR 5600 Environnement Ville et Société (EVS). Pour répondre aux enjeux des transitions écologique, énergétique et industrielle, le département GEO accompagne les acteurs des territoires (acteurs publics et privés) vers une meilleure prise en compte des enjeux environnementaux et de résilience territoriale. Il s'attache ainsi à apporter des solutions nouvelles en matière d'analyse, de modélisation et d'évaluation environnementale des systèmes industriels et territoriaux dans un double contexte d'industrie des futurs et de villes et territoires soutenables. 🏠 Contexte Présentation du sujet Le changement climatique met en lumière, comme l'a fait auparavant la crise COVID, les vulnérabilités et liens de dépendance généralisée de nos modes de vie envers les infrastructures, les chaînes de valeur, et modes d'organisation économique et technique, éléments souvent déconnectés de l'usager final, de ses besoins et des conditions d'occupation. Pour le secteur du bâtiment, Cimerman (2023) évoque une tendance depuis plusieurs décennies de « simplification cartésienne » de la conception et de l'opération du bâti. Celle-ci se traduit notamment par le développement d'un imaginaire de « bâtiment-machine », se traduisant par une superposition d'éléments techniques complexes (chauffage, ventilation, climatisation), susceptibles d'être pilotés au travers d'outils informatiques et d'une gestion centralisée optimisée (Cimerman, 2023). Face aux enjeux posés par le changement climatique, deux voies opposées d'adaptation du bâti se dessinent. La première, actuellement dominante, consiste à prolonger cet imaginaire de « bâtiment-machine », rationalisable, mesurable et optimisable, et ce notamment au travers du développement du « smart-building ». Cette approche technosolutionniste apporte des réponses clés-en-main (capteurs, outils de pilotage centralisés, etc.) aux gestionnaires et usagers de bâtiments. Néanmoins, elle présente certains défis pour leur maintenance et leur entretien. Nous pouvons citer le recours massif aux nouvelles technologies, coûteuses, complexes, rapidement obsolètes et dont la fabrication repose en grande partie sur des ressources finies. Cela pose de plus les questions centrales des compétences, de la délégation du savoir et des outils associés à des opérateurs experts externes. En contrepoint à la première voie, une seconde approche, encore marginale, émerge : celle d'un « bâtiment low-tech ». Popularisée ces dernières années en France par Philippe Bihouix (Bihouix, 2014), la low-tech questionne le rapport à la technologie et aux différentes formes de dépendances qu'elle génère (Tanguy et al., 2023). Dans le secteur du bâtiment, l'application de cette démarche renvoie souvent à la dépendance à la ressource (énergie et matière) : repenser les usages, l'origine des matériaux (réemployés, biosourcés) ou encore la simplicité de l'équipement utilisé. Bien que nécessaires, ces travaux s'intéressent pourtant peu à d'autres formes de dépendances associées à la technique, au titre desquelles nous pouvons citer la dépendance aux savoirs et aux formes d'organisation sociale et économique qui conditionnent l'adéquation, la pérennité et l'efficacité des solutions proposées. Cette thèse offre ainsi une immersion concrète dans les questions d'adaptation du parc bâti au changement climatique par la « lowtech » à l'interface entre sciences de l'ingénieur et sciences humaines et sociales. Les compétences et l'expérience acquises trouveront une résonance particulière dans un secteur en pleine mutation, où la maîtrise des dépendances techniques, économiques et organisationnelles devient un enjeu central pour la soutenabilité des bâtiments et de leur exploitation. Contexte scientifique La littérature consacrée à la low-tech s'est structurée ces dernières années autour d'une critique de la fuite en avant technologique et des dépendances qu'elle engendre (Bihouix, 2014 ; Tanguy et al., 2023). Appliquée au bâtiment, cette littérature reste toutefois majoritairement centrée sur la phase de conception et sur la dépendance à la ressource : sobriété énergétique, choix de matériaux biosourcés ou réemployés, réduction du niveau d'équipement technique. Deux angles morts en découlent. Le premier concerne la phase d'exploitation : la maintenance et l'entretien, qui représentent pourtant l'essentiel de la durée de vie d'un bâtiment et conditionnent la performance réelle des solutions installées, sont peu traités comme objet de recherche à part entière. Le second concerne la nature même des dépendances étudiées. Au-delà de la ressource, la conduite d'une opération de maintenance mobilise des savoirs et savoir-faire, des outils de diagnostic, des pièces détachées, des prestataires et des chaînes d'approvisionnement, ainsi que des cadres contractuels et réglementaires. Ces dépendances d’ordres cognitives, organisationnelles, économiques restent largement implicites et sous développées dans les travaux existants. La caractérisation de ces dépendances soulève par ailleurs une question d'échelle. Analysée au seul niveau du bâtiment, la maintenance apparaît comme une somme d'opérations techniques ; replacée à l'échelle urbaine, elle révèle des réseaux d'acteurs, des filières, des compétences localement disponibles ou absentes, et des effets de dépendance mutualisés. Contexte opérationnel Du côté des acteurs institutionnels et économiques, de nombreux outils accompagnent aujourd'hui la gestion technique du patrimoine bâti. Nous pouvons citer : les outils de gestion de maintenance assistée par ordinateur (GMAO) et les plateformes de gestion technique du bâtiment (GTB) ; les démarches de modélisation des données du bâtiment (BIM d'exploitation, jumeaux numériques) et les labels associés à la connectivité des bâtiments ; les contrats d'exploitation et de maintenance externalisés, et les dispositifs de garantie de performance énergétique ; les démarches et retours d'expérience issus de la mouvance low-tech (chantiers démonstrateurs, guides praticiens, réseaux associatifs). Ces dispositifs partagent une orientation commune : ils visent à optimiser la conduite de la maintenance, rarement à interroger les dépendances qu'elle installe. Les démarches low-tech, à l'inverse, portent cette interrogation mais restent au stade de l'expérimentation ponctuelle, sans cadre d'évaluation partagé ni capacité de généralisation à l'échelle d'un parc ou d'un territoire. Il en résulte, en l'état des connaissances aussi bien scientifiques qu'opérationnelles, qu'il n'existe pas de méthode permettant de rendre visibles et de qualifier les dépendances associées à la maintenance et à l'entretien des bâtiments, ni d'évaluer dans quelle mesure une approche low-tech permettrait de les réduire. 🎯  Ce que nous attendons de vous Démarche de la thèse L'objectif principal de cette thèse est de caractériser les apports d'une approche low-tech pour cartographier et maîtriser, sinon réduire, les différentes formes de dépendances associées à la maintenance et à l'entretien des bâtiments. Les dépendances analysées s'appuieront sur les techniques, pratiques, outils et réseaux en lien avec la maintenance qui seront mis en évidence dans les deux autres thèses du projet PERENNIS . Cette thèse s'inscrit donc en complète continuité de ces deux travaux. Dans un premier temps, il s'agira de construire un cadre d'analyse des dépendances liées à la maintenance du bâtiment, articulant quatre registres : les ressources (énergie, matière, pièces détachées), les savoirs et savoir-faire, les acteurs et leurs relations contractuelles, et les réseaux techniques et logistiques. Cette phase s'appuiera sur une revue de la littérature scientifique et « grise », sur un benchmark des pratiques et outils de maintenance existants, et sur des entretiens avec les acteurs du secteur (gestionnaires de patrimoine, bailleurs, mainteneurs, bureaux d'études, collectivités). Dans un deuxième temps, ce cadre sera mobilisé pour caractériser et rendre visibles les schémas de dépendance à l'échelle urbaine, sur un ou plusieurs territoires d'étude. Il s'agira notamment d'identifier les sources de données mobilisables pour objectiver ces schémas, de qualifier les points de fragilité et d'apprécier leur variabilité selon les typologies de bâtiments et les configurations d'acteurs. Dans un troisième temps, des stratégies prospectives low-tech de maintenance et d'entretien seront proposées et instruites. Il s'agira de construire des scénarios contrastés, d'évaluer leur capacité à réduire la vulnérabilité technique, économique et sociale des opérations de maintenance dans un contexte d'adaptation au changement climatique, et d'en discuter la faisabilité et l'acceptabilité avec les parties prenantes concernées. Verrous scientifiques : Définition et opérationnalisation de la notion de dépendance appliquée à la maintenance du bâti, au-delà de la seule dépendance à la ressource (savoirs, acteurs, organisations, réseaux) Caractérisation et représentation de schémas de dépendance à l'échelle urbaine, à partir de données hétérogènes et partiellement indisponibles Évaluation prospective de stratégies low-tech en l'absence de retours d'expérience consolidés et de métriques établies Articulation interdisciplinaire entre sciences de l'ingénieur et sciences humaines et sociales, et capacité à répliquer l'approche tout en visant la « parcimonie » des méthodes et modèles Objectifs de développement durable rattachés : ODD 11 – Villes et communautés durables · ODD 12 – Consommation et production responsables ODD 13 – Mesures relatives à la lutte contre les changements climatiques. 🔍 Ce que nous recherchons Formation : Bac +5 en ingénierie généraliste, sciences de l'environnement, génie civil ou énergétique du bâtiment, géographie/aménagement, ou discipline connexe. Une formation ou une sensibilité aux sciences humaines et sociales (sociologie des techniques, STS, économie de la fonctionnalité) serait un plus. Compétences requises : Méthodes qualitatives : conduite et analyse d'entretiens semi-directifs, observation de terrain, analyse de corpus documentaires. Analyse systémique et prospective : capacité à représenter un système sociotechnique, à construire et instruire des scénarios. Connaissance du bâtiment : compréhension du fonctionnement technique du bâti et de ses équipements, et des logiques d'exploitation et de maintenance. Traitement de données : aisance avec des données hétérogènes issues de sources variées ; la maîtrise d'outils de traitement (R, Python) ou de SIG (QGIS) serait appréciée. Gestion de projets : aptitude à structurer et mener des phases de projet de manière autonome, en articulation avec deux autres doctorants du projet. Langue : français courant et anglais opérationnel (capacité à lire des publications techniques et scientifiques en anglais). Profil recherché : individus responsables, proactifs, et dotés d'un esprit analytique, capables de faire preuve de rigueur scientifique. Personnes dynamiques, motivées par les enjeux environnementaux et par le questionnement critique de la technique. Capacité d'adaptation, goût pour le travail interdisciplinaire et collaboratif avec des acteurs variés. 📩 Candidatez dès maintenant !
